Do these ops stay inside a scope?

Source: R/sections.R
ops_within.Rd

Checks that every row a list of ops would touch lies inside a planner's scope – a list of targets, such as the sections they own. The answer is one row per op side that reaches outside it, so zero rows means every op stays inside.

Usage

ops_within(plan, ops, scope)

Arguments

plan

The MediaPlan the ops would be applied to.

ops

The ops, in any form build_scenario() takes them: a list of ops or a single op – plain lists, op constructors, or parsed from JSON – or a scenario's @edits record.

scope

The scope: a target, or a list of targets. Empty is the whole plan.

Value

A data frame with one row per op side that selects rows outside scope:

op

The op's position in ops.

side

"target", "from", "to" or "add".

line_items

A list column: the line items (line_item() at line_item_grain()) that side reaches outside the scope.

Details

Rows are resolved exactly as build_scenario() resolves them, in order: an add earlier in the list creates rows a later op may target, and a drop removes rows a later op can no longer reach. during, and a transfer's from_during / to_during, narrow each side as they do when the op is applied. An add is outside when the line item it creates does not match the scope.

A target that does not exist is refused here with the error build_scenario() gives. Ops that change which rows exist, when they run, or how they are bound (add, drop, shift, restage, rebound) are applied as they go, and refused as they would be there. Ops that only move money are not applied: they cannot change what a later op selects, and whether the money can move – past a floor, say – is build_scenario()'s question, whose answer must not hide this one. The scope is read leniently (match_rows() with strict = FALSE): it may name values the plan no longer has.

See also

match_rows(), rebase_check()

Examples

plan <- media_plan_from_df(
  data.frame(week = as.Date("2026-07-06"),
             channel = c("TV", "TV", "Search", "Social"),
             partner = c("NBC", "ESPN", "Google", "Meta"),
             planned_spend = c(50, 30, 40, 40)),
  grain = c("channel", "partner"), time = "week", name = "Q3"
)
video <- list(channel = "TV")

# inside: money moves between two TV partners
ops_within(plan, op_transfer(10, from = list(partner = "NBC"),
                             to = list(partner = "ESPN")), video)
#> [1] op         side       line_items
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

# outside: the money comes from Search
ops_within(plan, op_transfer(10, from = list(channel = "Search"),
                             to = list(partner = "ESPN")), video)
#>   op side      line_items
#> 1  1 from Search | Google
